R351 of 26 April 2011), Regs 13-16; Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 (FICA), as amended by the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022; Protection of Constitutional Democracy Against Related Activities Act 33 of 2004 (POCDATARA); CIPC Beneficial Ownership Filing Directive and prescribed CIPC BO forms.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in country of origin / issuing passport authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, or consular legalization if the country of origin is not a Hague Convention state

Foreign bank reference letter / AML clearance letter

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory negative screening of all directors, shareholders, and UBOs against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, UK HMT Consolidated List, EU Consolidated List, South African POCDATARA domestic terrorist lists, and FATF public statements. Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) and senior-management approval are mandatory where any foreign, domestic, or international-organization PEP is identified, in line with FIC Guidance Note 7. Source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation must be obtained for all PEPs and for Medium_Risk_Enhanced customers. Screening records and risk assessments must be retained for at least five years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) e-Services Portal, https://eservices.cipc.co.za (Name Reservation via form CoR 9.1 and entity name search)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name may be expressed in any one or more of the 12 official languages of South Africa and must be capable of being written in the Latin alphabet. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name, must not falsely imply connection with the State, must not be offensive or defamatory, and for a proprietary limited company must end with '(Proprietary) Limited' or the accepted abbreviation '(Pty) Ltd'. The full legal name may be supplemented by a separate trade name, but the registered name remains subject to CIPC approval.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a CIPC refusal under sections 12 or 14 of the Companies Act, the applicant may (1) submit written representations to CIPC for internal reconsideration within 20 business days of the refusal, attaching a revised name or supporting consent letters; (2) if the refusal is maintained, apply to the Companies Tribunal under section 160 for a formal determination within 20 business days of the refusal; and (3) alternatively or additionally, institute a judicial review in the High Court under the Promotion of Administrative Justice Act 3 of 2000 within 180 days of the administrative decision. A fresh name reservation application may be lodged in parallel to avoid project delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for this online consignment and second-hand luxury retail business, provided the virtual office supplier maintains a physical street address within South Africa (a PO Box or Postnet box alone is insufficient under section 23 of the Companies Act), accepts service of legal process, and maintains a document-handling facility for the statutory registers and beneficial-ownership records. A mail-forwarding-only address is not acceptable as the registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate: approximately 12-18% annual probability of an unannounced on-site compliance inspection by CIPC or an authorized regulatory inspector. SARS and FIC audits are normally document-driven with reasonable notice, but the registered office must be capable of producing the statutory records, minute books, and beneficial-ownership register for inspection on demand. Full digital archiving with same-day printable production at the registered address is the recommended mitigation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, ss. 13-16 (incorporation), ss. 19 and 66 (legal personality and Memorandum of Incorporation), ss. 50-66 (share capital and corporate governance), read with the Companies Regulations, 2011 (Form CoR 14.1), and the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022 (beneficial ownership filing).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), a public entity of the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) together with the executed Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI) and incorporators' declarations, lodged electronically through CIPC e-Services.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; a (Pty) Ltd may be incorporated with nil or nominal share capital, and South African law imposes no escrow or capital-deposit account requirement. The directors will place working capital as share premium or a shareholder loan for bank account opening purposes; subscriber shares may be issued partly paid.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the incorporation of the Company under the Companies Act 71 of 2008, as filed with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) by Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) together with the Memorandum of Incorporation, be and is hereby ratified and confirmed. RESOLVED FURTHER that 100 ordinary no-par-value shares be allotted and issued, fully paid up as agreed, to the subscriber shareholders. The registered office at the address recorded in the MOI is hereby adopted. The following officers are appointed: [Name], Director; [Name], Financial Director; and [Name], Accounting Officer. The Directors are authorised to effect SARS tax and VAT registration, open banking facilities, subscribe to the Stripe and Escrow-Pay payment rails, and complete all CIPC beneficial-ownership filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services (cipc.co.za), Companies Tribunal for appeals.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form CoR 9.1 electronically through CIPC e-Services stating preferred, second and third name choices; pay the online fee; the name is reserved for a renewable six-month period. Proceed to incorporation immediately after approval.
required_dossiers: Certified identity document or passport of each incorporator or authorised agent
Proof of payment of the name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, CIPC issues a query specifying grounds; re-apply with an alternative name or lodge a complaint with the Companies Tribunal under s. 160 of the Companies Act for review of the refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Memorandum of Incorporation and Governance Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Appointed legal practitioner or registered company formation agent; final approval by the founding shareholders.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the MOI in conformity with Schedule 1 of the Companies Act, incorporating articles governing share classes, director powers, quorum rules, indemnity clauses and the address of the registered office. Prepare shareholders' minutes electing the first directors and subscriber allotments.
required_dossiers: Draft MOI (custom articles or standard Schedule 1 form)
Engagement letter with the formation agent or attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Not applicable at this stage; the legal practitioner must correct drafting issues before filing to avoid a CIPC query, and any omission is fixed by a pre-registration amendment of the draft MOI.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing of Notice of Incorporation with CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), e-Services portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge Form CoR 14.1, the executed MOI, consents of the first directors, and the incorporators' declaration electronically via CIPC e-Services; pay the statutory filing fee; the system generates an acknowledgement and submission number. Retain the payment receipt and the submission acknowledgement.
required_dossiers: Certified identity documents or passports of incorporators and first directors
Directors' written consents to act (s. 51 of the Companies Act)
FICA-aligned KYC documents for AML verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to any CIPC query through e-Services, correcting the MOI or declarations; pay any shortfall in the fee; if incorporation is refused the applicant may within 60 days apply to the Companies Tribunal for review of the decision (s. 14(2) of the Companies Act).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Registration Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, download Form CoR 14.1A (Certificate of Incorporation) from CIPC e-Services; record the company registration number in the format YYYY/XXXXXX/07 and verify the exact legal name, date of incorporation and registered office as recorded on the certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Apply to CIPC under s. 24 of the Companies Act for rectification of the registration record if any particulars are incorrect; CIPC will re-issue an amended certificate of incorporation once the supporting evidence is accepted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and Employment Registration with SARS and Labour Authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) via eFiling; Department of Employment and Labour for COIDA.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Activate the automatic income tax registration resulting from CIPC data transfer by registering on SARS eFiling and obtaining the taxpayer PIN; register for VAT if taxable supplies exceed ZAR 1 million in a 12-month period or elect voluntary VAT; upon hiring staff, register for PAYE, UIF and SDL and register as an employer under COIDA.
required_dossiers: Bank account confirmation of the company's banking facilities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Escalate unresolved queries through SARS eFiling or a SARS branch; a registered tax practitioner may expedite the activation; any late-registration penalties should be addressed by prescribed SARS objection and remission procedures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Beneficial Ownership Filing and Establishment of Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC (beneficial ownership register); company secretarial function or accounting officer for statutory records.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 10 business days after registration, file the beneficial ownership particulars with CIPC via the mandatory electronic filing; prepare the statutory registers (members, directors, beneficial owners, share certificates and minute book), issue share certificates to the subscribers, and pass minutes covering the registered office and officer appointments.
required_dossiers: Beneficial ownership register prepared in accordance with s. 56 of the Companies Act
Register of members and register of directors
Minute book containing the first board resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late filing attracts administrative penalties; file the delinquent return immediately and, if applicable, submit a condonation request to CIPC; incorrect beneficial ownership data must be corrected by an amended filing within the prescribed 10-business-day period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: South African Police Service (SAPS), Second-Hand Goods Dealers Registration Office; Department of Employment and Labour for Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act (COIDA) compliance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Second-Hand Goods Dealer Registration Certificate (s. 7, Second-Hand Goods Act 6 of 2009). No separate industrial, trading or sectoral operating licence applies to pure online e-commerce consignment of vintage luxury goods under the Consumer Protection Act 68 of 2008 or the Business Act 71 of 1991.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - the e-commerce storage and dispatch of second-hand goods is not a listed activity under the NEMA EIA Regulations, 2014 (Listing Notices 1, 2 and 3); no environmental authorisation, basic assessment or full EIA report is required. Re-assess if a fulfilment warehouse exceeding approximately 2,000 m2 gross floor area is developed.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No manufacturing or effluent discharges arise. General waste must be removed by a licensed municipal or private waste carrier; returned electronics and e-waste are subject to the National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008 and its Norms and Standards; with respect to packaging placed on the market, Extended Producer Responsibility registration under s. 18 of the Waste Act may apply. No wastewater or VOC emission limits are triggered by this activity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For any fulfilment warehouse: fire-safety certificate from the local fire authority, electrical certificate of compliance, structural load inspection and OHSA 85 of 1993 risk assessment. If employees are engaged, register as an employer for COIDA and obtain a workplace certificate of compliance from an accredited health and safety agent. A pure home-office operation requires only general municipal health and safety compliance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); eFiling portal at https://www.sars.gov.za; company income tax reference number issued automatically through integrated CIPC incorporation filing (CoR14.1/CoR14.3) with subsequent VAT and PAYE registration administered via SARS eFiling.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a domestically incorporated (Pty) Ltd, the Income Tax reference number is auto-generated upon Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) registration through the National Companies Register integration with SARS. VAT registration is a separate application: submit VAT 101 with certified Memorandum of Incorporation, CIPC registration certificate, identity documents of directors, and SARS-held bank confirmation; foreign-owned entities must additionally appoint a SARS-recognised representative taxpayer, provide audited financial projections, and SARS may conduct a physical verification of the principal place of business. VAT registration is compulsory within 21 days once taxable turnover exceeds or is expected to exceed R1,000,000 in any 12-month period.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - resident South African company subject to corporate income tax at 27% on worldwide income (Income Tax Act 58 of 1962); no pass-through or transparency election available for (Pty) Ltd; capital gains included at an 80% inclusion rate; dividends distributed attract 20% Dividends Tax at shareholder level; territorial exemption does not apply to resident companies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa has no check-the-box entity classification regime. Available statutory elections relevant to an e-commerce luxury reseller: (i) s 9I headquarters company election subject to thresholds; (ii) VAT cash-basis accounting election (s 21(2) VAT Act, turnover not exceeding R2.5m); (iii) two-monthly VAT return filing election (s 27 VAT Act, turnover below R1.5m); (iv) hybrid mismatch rules (s 23N of Income Tax Act) apply mandatorily without elective opt-out; (v) participation exemption for foreign dividends (s 10B(2)) and CFC rules (s 9D) where offshore purchasing or fulfilment entities are used.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT - Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991 (SARS VAT 201 return regime)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory registration: R1,000,000 annual taxable turnover (actual over any consecutive 12-month period or expected in the next 12 months); voluntary registration available for persons making taxable supplies (the former R50,000 statutory minimum voluntary threshold was removed with effect from 1 May 2023); failure to register exposes the vendor to VAT on the first R1m of turnover plus penalties and interest.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or government clearance API mandate currently applies. SARS eFiling is the mandatory electronic channel for VAT returns. SARS eInvoicing is a voluntary structured electronic invoicing pilot using PEPPOL/UBL with optional digital signatures and SARS-side interoperability; tax invoices must contain the 15 prescribed particulars under s 20 VAT Act; credit notes must be issued within 21 days; online marketplace sellers must be prepared to provide CSV/XML transaction data during SARS data-matching audits.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Section 11(1)(a) VAT Act zero-rates the supply of movable second-hand luxury goods to a non-resident recipient where the goods are removed from South Africa within 90 days from the date of the tax invoice; the seller must retain prescribed documentary proof and receive full payment in South Africa within 12 months of export (VAT 'export' definition in s 1); related export logistics and fulfilment services supplied to non-residents may qualify for zero-rating under s 11(2)(l); for consignment sellers, the notional input tax claim under s 20(2) on second-hand goods acquired from non-vendors (15/115) remains available provided export substantiation is intact.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS may retrospectively claw back export zero-rating where the 90-day removal or 12-month payment conditions are not met, issuing an additional assessment with interest from the original due date; understatement penalties of up to 150% of the shortfall apply (s 223 Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011); criminal tax evasion convictions carry a fine and/or up to 5 years' imprisonment (s 235 TAA); false export declarations under the Customs and Excise Act 91 of 1964 attract confiscation, additional duty up to 100% of the value, and possible trader debarment; where notional input tax on second-hand goods is reversed, the clawback includes the deemed input VAT plus penalty; supporting export records must be retained for at least 5 years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) – Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv) is the sole exchange control authority, with day-to-day administration delegated to authorised dealer banks (commercial banks) under the Currency and Exchanges Manual and Exchange Control Circulars.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Africa is a 'Schedule C' exchange control country: the rand (ZAR) is convertible for trade and current-account transactions through authorised dealers without case-by-case SARB approval, subject to supporting documentation. Capital-account transactions require prior approval or reporting under the Currency and Exchanges Manual and Exchange Control Circulars. Profit remittance by non-resident shareholders is permitted upon completion of tax clearance and foreign investment registration; the local company must produce signed or audited financial statements or a dividend resolution, demonstrate that all export proceeds have been correctly surrendered or retained in approved foreign currency accounts, and maintain good SARS tax-compliance status. Shareholder capital may be repatriated after disinvestment reporting through the authorised dealer; shareholder loans must be registered and align with the SARB inward-loan guidelines before any interest or principal remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: All export proceeds, including service fees and consignment sales paid by foreign buyers, must be repatriated to South Africa within 90 days from the date of shipment or invoice unless an extended period is pre-approved by an authorised dealer or SARB FinSurv (normally up to 180 days, renewable). Mandatory conversion ratio: 100% of export proceeds must be sold into ZAR on the market through an authorised dealer, unless the entity holds a valid foreign currency account approval from an authorised dealer allowing retention of working capital. There is no statutory 50/50 split; the default is full conversion into ZAR, with only specifically approved importer/exporter arrangements allowed to retain foreign currency.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: The Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (inward capital injection) / Operational Account (multi-currency, ZAR)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: FirstRand Bank Limited (First National Bank – FNB)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account with integrated FX and trade finance
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account for settlement of e-commerce and consignment proceeds
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account with dedicated trade and treasury desk
Operational Account / Treasury and Wealth Account for high-net-worth cross-border trade flows

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium for direct core banking. Offshore EMIs (Wise, Airwallex, Stripe Treasury, EPX, Multitude) cannot act as SARB-authorised deposit-taking institutions or clearing banks in South Africa; they may only provide multi-currency collection and processing through a licensed partner bank. Such EMIs are legally viable for ancillary payment facilitation, but the entity must retain a primary ZAR operating account at an authorised dealer bank. Stripe is permissible as a merchant payment gateway for online card payments, and Escrow_Pay can function as a payment intermediary for consignment settlements, but all final clearing and SARB reporting must occur through the onshore commercial banking channel. A dedicated foreign currency account at an authorised dealer bank remains the regulatory-compliant mechanism for cross-border multi-currency liquidity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: South African banks operate under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act (FICA) and their own client-acceptance policies. For a newly formed Pty Ltd, at least one director or an MOI-authorised representative must be physically present for identity verification, unless the bank offers approved remote digital onboarding via video KYC and the entity's risk profile fits the bank's digital tolerance. Non-resident directors generally must appear for a face-to-face interview at a branch, or provide a notarised or apostilled identification pack and attend a secure video interview where the specific bank permits digitally enabled onboarding. Physical presence remains the default for businesses rated 'Medium_Risk_Enhanced' and for entities lacking an existing banking relationship. The company must also submit its registration certificate, Memorandum of Incorporation, board resolution, register of directors, final beneficial ownership disclosure, physical address verification, and detailed business plan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident discretionary majority shareholder and complex ultimate beneficial ownership chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder register, corporate registry extract showing all natural-person beneficial owners, trust deed or foundation deed, identification of every individual holding 25% or more economic interest, signed source-of-wealth declaration, and audited financial statements of the parent entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Consignment model with third-party seller remittances creating potential commingling of funds and invoice mismatch
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed consignment agreements, authenticated luxury-good provenance certificates, mirrored consignor settlement reports, fee and commission schedules, buyer payment evidence from gateways, and bank merchant settlement statements mapping each consignor's entitlement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border high-value secondhand luxury goods flagged as high-value commodity-crime typology
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: AML/CFT compliance manual, transaction monitoring policies, customer due diligence and enhanced due diligence files for consignors and consignees, red-flag escalation logs, board-approved entity-level risk assessment, FIC registration confirmation if the entity qualifies as an accountable institution, and independent audit assurance report on internal controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Export proceeds not reconcilable with customs declarations and shipping documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Customs SAD500 export declarations, bills of lading, commercial invoices, packing lists, delivery notes, inward payment reference (CMS report from the authorised dealer), and an exporter ledger demonstrating 90-day repatriation and full conversion compliance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident equity capital must be wired by SWIFT MT103 from the founding shareholder's foreign bank account to a designated 'Capital Escrow Account' at an authorised dealer bank. The wire instruction must state the purpose as 'share subscription – inward foreign investment' and be accompanied by the SARB Form FI (inward investment report), incorporation certificate, English version of the Memorandum of Incorporation, share-allocation resolution, and audited financial statements if the company is already trading. Upon receipt, the authorised dealer issues a Foreign Investment Realisation Certificate or an FI reference number, which is mandatory for future dividend remittance and disinvestment. If the funding is structured as a shareholder loan, a formal loan agreement, SARB inward-loan application, corporates registration form, and the authorised dealer's approval letter must be completed before drawdown. Receiving capital through Stripe, Escrow_Pay, or offshore EMIs is not acceptable for regulatory capital; such channels may only be used for ordinary trade receivables and not for equity or quasi-equity injections.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade-settlement rails for this business comprise: (i) SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers via the authorised dealer bank for direct supplier and refund payments to foreign counterparties; (ii) commercial Letters of Credit (L/C) for high-value vintage stock imports and structured consignments, opened with the authorised dealer and confirmed by a foreign correspondent bank; (iii) domestic ZAR interbank clearing through SAMOS (South African Multiple Option Settlement) for payouts to local consignors and vendors; and (iv) gateway-based disbursements via Stripe and Escrow_Pay for consumer refunds and seller settlements, provided the funds are ultimately cleared into and from the bank's ZAR operating account. Every outward payment must be matched to underlying invoices, customs declarations, refund notifications, or settlement contracts; the authorised dealer will apply exchange-control verification and SARB cross-border payment reporting where applicable. Direct use of offshore EMI accounts as the principal clearing venue is not compliant unless the arrangement is specifically approved and reported through the authorised dealer.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forward contracts (USD/ZAR, EUR/ZAR) – permitted through an authorised dealer bank, must be supported by documented underlying trade or capital exposure and cannot be speculative.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts – executable through a South African authorised dealer as principal in the non-deliverable ZAR offshore market for hedging where physical settlement is not required.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) – permitted for long-term foreign-currency debt or capital commitments, requiring prudent tenor alignment and appropriate SARB/FinSurv notification through the authorised dealer.

Zero-cost collar and option spread strategies – permissible when used exclusively for hedging of committed cross-border receipts or payments, with no speculative intent, and executed through the authorised dealer's treasury desk.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Companies Act s.33) with registered address, directors, secretary and financial year-end data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary of the company's incorporation date, every year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers CIPC penalty of approx. ZAR 500 (USD 27); failure to file for two consecutive years places the company in 'delinquent' status and exposes it to administrative strike-off under s.82(3) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 after CIPC notice; reinstatement requires CIPC application, settlement of arrears and restoration of good standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (AFS) and Independent Review or Audit Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: CIPC (submitted with Annual Return); South African Revenue Service (SARS) (supporting income tax assessment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AFS must be prepared within 6 months of the company's financial year-end and filed with CIPC together with the Annual Return (i.e., within 30 business days of registration anniversary)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CIPC cannot process the Annual Return without AFS where Public Interest Score (PIS) is 100 or more; non-compliance attracts the same late penalty and two-year strike-off risk, plus bank-covenant default in lending and payment-escrow arrangements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Register and Annual Confirmation Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually with the Annual Return; any share transfer or beneficial ownership change must be lodged within 30 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to ZAR 1,000,000 (approx. USD 54,000) under the Companies Act; directors may be held personally liable; enforcement integrates with FIC Act AML obligations for a Medium_Risk_Enhanced online luxury-resale merchant.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (ITR14) and Provisional Tax Payments
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: ITR14 due within 12 months of financial year-end (per SARS auto-assessment); provisional tax: first payment 6 months after year start, second payment by financial year-end, top-up payment 6 months after year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Understatement penalty of 10% (20% for gross negligence), interest of 10% p.a. on outstanding amounts, and possible criminal prosecution for repeated non-filing, plus SARS set-off against refunds.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: B-BBEE Annual Compliance Report and Certificate (turnover-dependent; mandatory only if annual turnover equals or exceeds ZAR 10 million)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 6 months after the end of the company's financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-reporting entities are named on the Commission compliance register and risk exclusion from public-sector contracts and major corporate supply chains; no strike-off effect but commercial debarment risk is significant.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent external audit if the Public Interest Score (PIS) is 350 or more; independent review by a registered accounting practitioner required if PIS is between 100 and 349; PIS below 100 with internally compiled AFS is exempt from both audit and independent review (Companies Act s.30 read with Companies Regulations 26-29).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for listed and public-interest entities; IFRS for SMEs permitted and commonly applied by private (Pty) Ltd companies; CIPC and SAICA guidance require full IFRS where the company is listed or holds material public interest.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Register of Beneficial Ownership (ROE) must be maintained and filed with CIPC annually with the Annual Return; any shareholding transfer, nominee collapse, or change in beneficial ownership must be reflected in the register and lodged with CIPC within 30 days of the event; the company must identify the ultimate natural-person owner and document the chain of control; failure to keep the ROE accurate for more than 30 days is an offence under the amended Companies Act.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of shareholders' and directors' meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - 700 per annum (CIPC-accredited registered office address and company secretarial maintenance retainer; excludes audit fees)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,800 - 5,000 for full IFRS audit; USD 800 - 2,200 for independent review (typical small-to-mid-market Pty Ltd)
